title: Oracle Stock News (Oct 14, 2026): ORCL Rises 4.2% to $143.20
summary: Oracle (ORCL) closed at $143.20 on Oct 13, 2026, up 4.23%, on a day of Project Jupiter power filings. What moved the stock and the risks.
body_markdown:
Even after the gain, the stock sits 55.60% below its 52-week high of $322.54 and 25.07% above its 52-week low of $114.50.


## Why Oracle Stock Rose


None of the reports fetched for this article tied Tuesday's 4.23% gain to a specific company event, so the move is best read against Oracle's news flow that day and a flat market.


The main company news concerned power for Project Jupiter. Per[MT Newswires](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oracle-proposes-paying-100-million-142507767.html) , Oracle proposed an energy service agreement with El Paso Electric under which it expects to pay $10 million a year for 10 years, $100 million in total, even if its usage falls below contracted levels. A separate proposal would give up to $55 million a year in bill credits for up to three years to the utility's New Mexico residential and small business customers. As reported by[Stocktwits](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oracle-proposes-55m-annual-power-152522222.html) , Oracle said its primary power plan is unchanged, with Bloom Energy's fuel cell microgrid as the main supply. "There is no change to our plan," the company said.


According to[Investing.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/oracle-urges-ferc-expedite-mexico-215237380.html) , Oracle also urged the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in a Tuesday letter to expedite approval of the 17.8-mile Green Chile gas pipeline that would feed the campus microgrid.


Earlier the same day, per[MT Newswires](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/marvell-microsoft-oracle-form-data-132439267.html) , Marvell, Microsoft and Oracle set up an Open Compute Project working group to standardize hardware security modules built directly into data center servers.


## ORCL Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Oracle reaffirmed that its Bloom Energy fuel cell plan remains the main power source for Project Jupiter, according to Stocktwits.
- The El Paso Electric agreement would cover late-stage construction, initial commissioning and emergency backup power for the campus, as reported by Stocktwits.
- The new security working group with Microsoft and Marvell targets cryptographic key protection for cloud and hyperscale infrastructure, per MT Newswires.


### Risks


- The Green Chile pipeline's timeline has slipped to February 2027 from an initial August target after local opposition forced a reroute, according to Investing.com.
- Environmental groups and New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez want regulators to review the combined footprint of the data center and pipeline, per Investing.com.
- Oracle would owe the $100 million under the proposed agreement even if its power usage runs below contracted levels, per MT Newswires.
- The stock remains 55.60% below its 52-week high, and Stocktwits noted it was down nearly 29% year to date before Tuesday's close.
